content:
RetroLine is a small USB-C-powered adapter with an RJ-11 phone jack that allows you to connect a retro rotary dial (pulse) and touch-tone (DTMF) phone and make or receive calls over Bluetooth through your smartphone. The company, Indigo Telephony, says it behaves like a real line. Users can pick their country, and the RetroLine box matches the dial, busy and ringback tones, ring cadence, and Caller ID format. The bells inside older 1970s phones can also ring. RetroLine key features and specifications: SoC – Not disclosed. The company only mentions a “fast microcontroller”, and I suspect it may be an ESP32. Storage – MicroSD card slot for call recording, hold music, sound-board clips, and system logs Wireless Bluetooth for connection to your smartphone WiFi for web dashboard Phone connector – RJ-11 jack compatible with rotary dial (pulse) and touch-tone (DTMF) phones Audio High-fidelity audio codec Custom hold music (WAV or MP3) [...]
